statement: For an unpenalized regression under prediction, multiplying its coefficients by the calibration slope — the bootstrap's optimism-corrected slope when the bootstrap ran, else the out-of-fold cross-validated slope — and re-estimating the intercept with the shrunk linear predictor as an offset is a sound model update that corrects for overfitting.
regime: Prediction; unpenalized regression family; numeric or binary outcome
decision: The model-updating offer (uniform shrinkage) and the deployed coefficients
user_sees: "The regression's coefficients were shrunk by the calibration slope as model updating, and its intercept re-estimated with the shrunk linear predictor as an offset (TRIPOD+AI 12f; Steyerberg 2019)."
claimed_basis: Collins et al., BMJ 2024 (optimism-corrected slope as shrinkage factor); Steyerberg 2019 §13.2; Van Houwelingen & le Cessie 1990.
notes: [part id F2-026] test_explore_4_decision_curve.py::test_4_shrinkage_by_the_calibration_slope_re_estimates_the_intercept_as_r_does is implementation fidelity. Collins specifies the optimism-corrected slope; the out-of-fold slope fallback (slope_of :368) comes from fold models fit on (K−1)/K of the rows, which overfit more than the full model, so it may over-shrink. For an imbalance-corrected model the slope multiplies the recalibrated coefficients (:339). [Merged F5-018 at turbotab/core/stages/evaluation.py:400-464 (_shrinkage, updates_by_shrinkage); turbotab/core/models/decision_curve.py:356 (shrinkage), :368 (slope_of); linear.…; its basis: Collins et al. BMJ 2024 ('the value of optimism corrected calibration slope can be used to adjust the model ... as shrinkage factor'); Steyerberg; TRIPOD+AI 12f; MODEL_FAMILY_CONTRACT C9.; its notes: turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_explore_4_decision_curve.py::test_4_shrinkage_by_the_calibration_slope_re_estimates_the_intercept_as_r_does checks the arithmetic against R, not that it improves calibration. The out-of-fold slope comes from models fit on (K-1)/K of the rows, so applying it to the all-rows model over-shrinks slightly; the offer appears even if the slope exceeds 1. Overlaps fork F2 (decision_curve.…] [Merged F4-033 at turbotab/core/models/linear.py:151; its basis: MODEL_FAMILY_CONTRACT C9; WAVE_C6A_PLAN §5 ruling 7 (ridge.py:37-38); no citation in these files.; its notes: Implementation in stages/evaluation.py:_shrinkage (another fork). ridge.py:138 updating = (). Elastic net and Huber also declare none, without stated reason.]

statement: For the proportional-odds model, Wald intervals from the inverse observed information are valid for independent rows, and when rows repeat within units the CR1 sandwich over units' summed scores with a G/(G−1) correction and a t(G−1) reference gives valid 95% intervals (no interval below the unit floor).
regime: inference; ordinal outcome; independent rows or rows clustered by unit
decision: interval method for the ordinal coefficient table
user_sees: Caption: "95% intervals cluster-robust by `{unit}` (sandwich over G = {G} units with the G/(G − 1) correction, Stata's vce(cluster)), on t({G−1})." or "95% Wald intervals from the model's information."
claimed_basis: Cameron & Miller 2015 §VI ("at a minimum one should use the T(G − 1) distribution"); MASS::polr / statsmodels OrderedModel for the Wald case.
notes: [part id F4-037] acceptance/test_wp12a_ordinal.py::test_2_cluster_robust_intervals_match_statsmodels_sandwich_on_t_g_minus_1 and ::test_2_reproduces_mass_polr_published_housing_fit check computation against implementations, not coverage. Linear family uses CR2 + Bell–McCaffrey for the same situation (linear.py:5-8), so the ordinal table uses a weaker small-G correction; unit floor from inference.floor_refusal (outside area A).

statement: Under the dietary lens, when the exposure's Pearson correlation with total energy is 0.3 or more in absolute value, the choice of energy model (substitution at fixed energy versus addition) changes what the exposure's coefficient means, so the noticing is graded 'act on it' (changes the question) and decided at the energy-model question; below 0.3 no such noticing is raised.
regime: Dietary lens; exposure and an energy column both present; Estimate or Describe (also measured under Predict when the lens is dietary)
decision: Whether the energy-carries-the-nutrient noticing fires and is a Decide routed to energy_adjustment
user_sees: "`sugar` moves with `kcal` at r = 0.45: whether its coefficient means a swap at the same energy or eating more changes what the estimate is."
claimed_basis: Code comment: 'BLUEPRINT §14 rule 1: a nutrient correlated with total energy at r >= 0.3 rides on it'; SURFACING_POLICY §2.1 (substitution versus addition is changes_question)
notes: [part id F6-005] Also materiality.py:648-674 (energy_noticing). BLUEPRINT §14 rule 1 (BLUEPRINT.md:547-549) uses r >= 0.3 as value evidence that a column is a nutrient (recognizer confidence), not as a threshold for when the energy model changes the estimand; the citation is repurposed. Substitution versus addition changes the coefficient's meaning at any r; the 0.3 cut only decides whether to raise it. test_materiality_dietary_proof.py::test_energy_carries_the_nutrient_changes_the_question pins behavior on the fixture.

statement: Under inference, quintiles of a continuous exposure estimate a coarser contrast rather than a false number: they discard the variation within each fifth and assume a step at each cut. They therefore rank below the spline (and the straight line) but are not blocked.
decision: functional form of a continuous exposure or confounder (MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 5)
user_sees: Quintiles (rank lower): "Weaker for inference: cutting a continuous intake into fifths discards the variation within each fifth and assumes a step at each cut..."
claimed_basis: MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 2 ("a coarser contrast, not a false number"); NUTRITION_PACK §07G; Turner 2010 (contract :2537, "the field's primary-analysis convention")
notes: For a confounder the order is spline, linear, categories, quintiles, optimal (:1090). Doc: MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 2 (quintiles rank lower, not blocked; spline first; optimal cut points and <=3-group confounders block-and-record, see S2-020, S2-021).

statement: Survey weights and PSUs given without a strata column give intervals that treat the PSUs as unstratified, which are too narrow where people were sampled in clusters, so the answer is blocked until the user attests that the table has no strata column.
regime: set_survey population with a weight and PSU but no strata
user_sees: No strata is named. Weights correct the estimate, not its interval: the intervals would treat the PSUs as unstratified, and where people were sampled in clusters they are too narrow.
notes: Same refusal as S4-018, strata branch. Ignoring stratification with PSUs present usually overstates the with-replacement variance (conservative), so 'too narrow' does not follow for missing strata. Once attested, build_design (models/survey.py:153-160) puts every row in one stratum and keys PSUs by their code alone, so NHANES SDMVPSU codes 1/2 reused across strata collapse into two PSUs (df = 1).

statement: A proportional-hazards failure of the exposure is declared when the cox.zph score test of the exposure's own term (not the global test or the covariates' terms) has p < 0.05, the customary level; the failure then carries response exits.
decision: whether the PH check is 'failed' and response exits are offered
user_sees: The hazard ratio of what you study changes over follow-up (chi2(1) = ..., p = ..., below the customary 0.05): the reported ratio is an average over follow-up.
claimed_basis: PH_ALPHA = 0.05 'at the customary level' (turbotab/core/models/effects.py:88); MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 11
notes: test_estimand_4_diagnostics.py::test_4_proportional_hazards_agree_with_cox_zph asserts one simulated non-PH exposure is detected (power on one case), not the rule. A significance test at large n flags trivial departures and at small n misses large ones; covariates' PH failures do not fail the check. Inconsistent thresholds: the fit stage's proportional-hazards warning uses p < 0.01/P (models/survival.py:518, S7-042), this stage p < 0.05 on the exposure's term.

statement: With a log or a nonlinear form of a substituted energy component, moving k kcal no longer has one effect per kcal. Each person's effect depends on k and their own intake, so each point of the substitution curve is an average over the analyzed rows at that k, not a coefficient difference. An all-components contrast is undefined on logged components.
regime: substitution curve with log or spline on donor or recipient
user_sees: "With a nonlinear form of `fat_g`, moving k kcal no longer has one effect per kcal: each person's effect depends on k and on their own intake, so each point ... is an average ..."
claimed_basis: MODELING_SEQUENCE §2 Corrected ("Draft 1 said 'ratio rather than difference'; that was wrong")
notes: test_form_8 checks the label strings only. Doc: MODELING_SEQUENCE §2 (Corrected): the curve is labeled as an average over the stated population at the stated k, and 'the all-components contrast is undefined on logged components'; draft 1's 'ratio rather than difference' was withdrawn as wrong.

statement: Under the metabolomics, genomics or survey lens alone, a yes/no outcome with no numeric column that reads as a follow-up time is a status at sampling and is correctly analyzed as counted over one period for everyone (a binary model), without asking about follow-up.
regime: Binary outcome; assay or survey lens only (not clinical/dietary); no recognized follow-up column
decision: Whether the follow-up question is asked; binary vs time-to-event analysis
user_sees: "no numeric column reads as a follow-up time, and under this lens a yes/no outcome is a status at sampling, so it is read as counted over one period for everyone." (StatedSkip with 'Ask me anyway')
notes: Crosswalk default:follow_up_one_period (Confirm). Under clinical/dietary lenses (FOLLOWED_LENSES) or no lens the question is always asked. The claim rests on the lens, not on the data. | Inventory source id: CW-002.

statement: Total energy's unit is settled by its values only when its median ratio to the macronutrients' Atwater reconstruction lies within 0.90-1.10 (kcal, over the same days the macronutrients span); a ratio within 5% of 4.184 x N or of N (N >= 2) could be kJ or an N-day kcal total (a 4-day kcal total reads 4.00, within 5% of kJ's 4.184), so the unit and the day count are asked together with the fitting readings offered, and a ratio near 1 never settles how many days the values span.
regime: Dietary data with total energy and at least two macronutrient totals in grams.
decision: Energy unit/day count used by intake screens and energy methods.
user_sees: "is about 4.00x the energy its macronutrients carry: kJ or kcal over 4 days, which the values cannot tell apart"
claimed_basis: NUTRITION_PACK §01 (Atwater reconstruction; pass band 0.90-1.10); RATIO_TOLERANCE 0.05 = 'the pack's band around the kJ factor (nutrition._reconstruct)'; fifth gate (a 4-day record).
notes: unit_day_candidates readings.py:870 (MAX_TOTAL_DAYS 31); KIND_RULES unit:energy readings.py:1222; consumers stages.proposals:energy_unit_reading and decisions:_screens_wait_for_the_unit. | Inventory source id: F3-026.

statement: The same kind of measurement taken at baseline beside an outcome measured over follow-up (HbA1c beside incident diabetes, blood pressure beside incident hypertension, LDL beside LDL at 12 months) precedes the outcome, can predict it, and may have changed or been changed by the diet, so it takes the declared with-and-without pair rather than being left out; beside a change-since-baseline outcome, adjusting for a baseline the exposure may have changed can itself bias the analysis, so neither model alone is the default.
regime: Inference with a follow-up outcome (time-to-event, incident binary, or follow-up/change/time-since-baseline outcome); covariate of the outcome's group.
decision: Pre-filled adjustment answers (with-and-without pair) for a baseline level of the outcome's kind.
user_sees: "a level of the outcome `incident_diabetes`'s own kind (glycemic) measured at baseline with what you study, so before the event: no consequence of the event, and it can predict it; ... declared wit...
claimed_basis: NUTRITION_PACK §08; Schisterman 2009; Glymour et al. 2005 Am J Epidemiol 162:267-278 (baseline adjustment in change analyses); MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 step 3.
notes: test_leash.py::test_1_a_baseline_level_of_the_outcomes_kind_beside_an_incident_event_is_the_pair uses a simulation (_incident_cohort) but asserts the pair is offered, not that it is the right default. For incident-event outcomes the standard practice is usually to adjust for baseline levels (or exclude prevalent cases); the pair puts 'without' as primary. | Merged duplicates: F1-028 at turbotab/core/routing_leash.py:99-105. | Inventory source id: F3-046.

statement: The precision of a held-out AUC is approximated by Hanley & McNeil's (1982) standard error at an assumed AUC of 0.75 for the held-out events and non-events, and the precision of a held-out macro-F1 by a proportion's worst-case 95% interval (±1.96·√(0.25/k)) on the rarest class's k held-out rows.
regime: binary or multiclass outcome; split question before any fit
decision: The precision shown beside each holdout size
user_sees: "About {n} held-out rows, {k} in the rarer class: AUC known to about ±0.xx." / "… macro-F1 known to about ±0.xx."
claimed_basis: Hanley & McNeil 1982, Radiology 143:29–36 for the AUC; none stated for the macro-F1 approximation.
notes: PRECISION_NOTE seal.py:616-619. The macro-F1 rule is ad hoc. Ordinal: no closed form is claimed and none is shown. | Inventory source id: F1-021.

statement: A cross-validated or held-out R² for a regression outcome is measured against the training rows' mean and pooled over every out-of-fold prediction.
user_sees: R² was measured against the training rows' mean and pooled over every out-of-fold prediction
notes: Conflicts with BEATS_PREDICT §17 ruling 7 (D-025), which computes the opened cycle's R² against the cycle's own mean; test_modeling.py:213 asserts the training-mean convention.

statement: An eligibility cut chosen by looking at the outcome is data-driven selection with its own bias, so the eligibility question withholds the outcome's distribution and a custom range never applies to the outcome.
user_sees: A restriction comes from your research question, so the outcome's distribution is not shown here.

user_sees: These describe how each model turns measures into estimates, not what changing a measure would do.
claimed_basis: Lundberg & Lee 2017; Apley & Zhu 2020; Molnar et al. 2022
notes: §6 item 6 (line 1067); FOUNDATION §8 floor. The 0.7 threshold is unsourced.
